description: A version is proposed only once it has been public for seven days, so that a release pulled or fixed in its first week never reaches a branch. internalChecksFilter is already strict by default; it is stated so that the wait is read here as holding back the branch and the pull request themselves, not only a status check on them

customManagers.description: porkadot keeps the versions it installs in default.yaml, which no manager reads. A comment on the line above each version says where to look it up: `# renovate: datasource=<datasource> depName=<name>`, optionally followed by packageName=, versioning= and extractVersion= in that order. The version is the value of the key on the next line, without its quotes. A version is tracked by writing the comment, not by adding a manager here

Some images are written directly into the templates instead of default.yaml. They carry the same comment above the image line, written as an ERB comment (`<%-# renovate: ... -%>`) so that it does not appear in the rendered manifests. The version is the tag of the image on the next line
matchStrings: <%-# renovate: datasource=(?<datasource>\S+) depName=(?<depName>\S+)(?: packageName=(?<packageName>\S+))?(?: versioning=(?<versioning>\S+))?(?: extractVersion=(?<extractVersion>\S+))? -%>\n\s*image: [^\s:]+:(?<currentValue>\S+)

customManagers.description: The gem's dependencies are in the gemspec. The bundler manager reads only the Gemfile, which here says just `gemspec`, and Gemfile.lock is not committed, so no other manager reads them. Each line already names the gem and its range, so it is read directly; a comment would only repeat the name. The ranges belong to a library, so a pull request appears only when a release falls outside one
CI installs the tools some tests need by a version set in the workflow's env. The same comment as in default.yaml sits on the line above each one, and the version is the value on the next line

packageRules.description: Otherwise Renovate offers only the newest release, which folds a patch into the minor after it. With the minor disabled below, the patch would be dropped too. Kept separate, the newest patch of the current minor is offered on its own

These follow the Kubernetes minor version. Each porkadot release supports one Kubernetes minor, and the minor is raised by hand together with the porkadot release that supports it, so only patch releases are proposed. Before each etcd minor upgrade, etcd has to be on a recent enough patch release (3.5.26 or later before 3.6, 3.6.11 or later before 3.7). A patch-only update never crosses a minor, so it does not run into this
flannel's daemon and CNI plugin are released together, and each flannel release names the plugin it was tested with, so both are updated on one branch

The CNI plugin's tags are a plugins version followed by -flannelN, where N counts flannel's builds of that version. Docker versioning reads the suffix as a variant and would offer only tags with the same -flannelN. Read as a build number, a newer build of the same plugins version is offered too
These images are the user's own. The wait protects against a broken release published by someone else, and ghcr.io gives no release time to wait on, so these images are exempt

registry.k8s.io gives no release time, so the wait would hold these images back for good. etcd is read as an image because its tag ends in a -N suffix, which counts Kubernetes' rebuilds and is missing from the etcd releases. Only etcd patch releases are proposed, and each one goes through the dev cluster before a porkadot release. The amd64-only autoscaler name has had no new tag since 1.8.1, so letting it through without a release time cannot bring in a fresh release

MetalLB's template is rendered from the kustomizations in hack/metallb, which the kustomize manager already reads, so the image tags in the rendered template are not tracked. Both kustomizations name the same release and are updated together. The pull request changes only the ref; run hack/update-metallb.sh on its branch to render the template and the CRDs from the new release

Patch, digest and pinning updates are merged by Renovate itself once the pull request's checks pass. CI runs bundle exec rake test on every pull request, with no paths filter, so every branch Renovate opens is tested before it is merged. platformAutomerge is off so that the merge waits for those checks without relying on the repository's auto-merge setting or branch protection. Minor and major updates only open a pull request. Merged updates reach a release through the weekly release workflow, which tags the next patch version when Renovate's commits are all there is since the latest tag

A MetalLB update is not finished by Renovate's pull request: it changes only the ref, and hack/update-metallb.sh has to be run on the branch to render the template and the CRDs. Merged as it is, the ref would name a release that porkadot does not install, and the tests would still pass. So even a patch update waits to be merged by hand

Workflows are already read by the github-actions manager. Grouping them keeps a handful of actions from arriving as a handful of pull requests, since they are updated together and reviewed the same way
